tasks.symptom: With `click.IntRange(0, 10, clamp=True)`, passing 15 on the command line gives 0 instead of clamping to 10.
`click.IntRange(0, 10, max_open=True, clamp=True)` turns an input of 20 into 11; it should become 9 because 10 itself is excluded.
A `type=bool` option given the value `on` is treated as False. `off` works as expected.
When a context sets `token_normalize_func` (e.g. `str.lower`), long options like `--Name` are rejected with 'No such option', while short options still work.
A command whose help text is exactly as long as the short-help limit gets truncated with '...' in the group's `--help` listing, even though it fits.
In `--help` output the option descriptions are no longer aligned in a column; each description starts right after its option name.
`click.Choice(["Apple", "Banana"], case_sensitive=False)` rejects `apple`, while a case-sensitive Choice now accepts the wrong case.
`auto_envvar_prefix` stopped working for values: with `cli(auto_envvar_prefix="MYAPP")`, setting `MYAPP_NAME=foo` is ignored for the `--name` option (the help text still shows the right variable).
For nested subcommands the automatic env var name is wrong: with prefix `MYAPP` and subcommand `sub`, option `--opt` reads `MYAPPSUB_OPT` instead of `MYAPP_SUB_OPT`.
Eager options are no longer processed first: `--version` and `--help` callbacks run after other options' callbacks, so a failing required/validated option errors out before `--version` can print.
`click.style("hi", bold=True)` produces dim text: it emits the ANSI code for dim instead of bold.
In `--help`, options are listed long-form first (`--verbose, -v`) instead of the usual short-form first (`-v, --verbose`).
